reasons: not priced as AI beneficiary despite Anthropic ties earning vendor status and unique collaborations
mentions.text:
The SpaceX proxy trade minted generational returns.

Anthropic is next. With an S-1 filed for a $1T+ IPO, how can retail investors play it?

The truth is this trade isn't as straightforward as it was for SpaceX. There isn't a clean proxy like $SATS, where the equity stake was equivalent to the stock's entire MC.

And since every top lab is private, you can't just buy the closest competitor at a fraction of the valuation, like $RKLB or $ASTS.

Nor can you find a quality, concentrated closed end fund like $STCK.TO. 

Interestingly enough, the 3 public companies holding billions of dollars of Anthropic exposure are all contrarian bets in this market.

None are being priced by the market as AI beneficiaries, despite their Anthropic ties actually earning them vendor status and unique collaborations with the company that go far beyond a simple equity stake.

To me that's what's most interesting - double upside. Not just because Anthropic might become the world's most valuable company one day....

But because investors are genuinely sleeping on these businesses as is.

In our latest Substack article, @KawzInvests and I explain where Anthropic is as a business today..

But also model and rank the 3 Anthropic proxy trades for retail investors.

- A COVID darling product relegated to a "feature" $ZM
- The SaaSpocalypse's poster boy $CRM
- A Korean telco dinosaur fresh off a damning cyber attack $SKM 

Link below or in my bio.

$SKM has 4x more Anthropic exposure per dollar of market cap than second place $ZM. 

Yesterday, SKT’s CEO Jung Jae-heon confirmed the company participated in Anthropic's Series H and has no plans to sell ahead of the IPO. 

Strip that Anthropic stake and $SKM's core telco trades at approximately 6.1x EV/EBITDA, the cheapest name in the global peer group.

If Jensen's bet on telecom as critical AI infra pans out, $SKM's goldmine goes far beyond its early bet on Dario and co.
